title: Venezuelan Yeasty Pork Knuckle Empanadas
description: Delicate, flaky pastry pockets filled with slow-cooked pork knuckle in a rich, yeasty sauce, a crowd-pleaser from Venezuela.
instructions: Combine flour, lard or shortening, warm water, yeast, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Mix until dough comes together in a shaggy mass, then knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Bake dough for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
Meanwhile, braise pork knuckle in a large Dutch oven with onion, garlic, and enough water to cover.
Simmer for 2-3 hours, or until pork is tender and easily shreds with a fork.
Strain braising liquid and discard solids, then stir in sour cream and butter.
Roll out chilled dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a spoonful of braised pork knuckle in the center of each dough circle.
Fold dough over filling to form a half-moon shape, and press edges to seal.
Use a fork to crimp edges and create a decorative border.
Brush tops with a little water and sprinkle with cilantro.
